3.speaker: Iosef Lancea
3.text: ”Welcome to the Ministry of Defense, Mr. President. Let's go to my office.“

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: At the entrance, I was greeted by Iosef and his military entourage of young officers.

8.speaker: Iosef Lancea
8.text: ”You are overstepping and interrupting a personal meeting between me and the President.“

9.speaker: Player
9.text: ”Valken has a point. The military needs to be on the same page on any changes.“

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: Iosef checked his folder before looking at me.

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: A strong knock on the door was heard and the Chief of the Armed Forces; Valken Kruger walked in quickly with a frown.

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: We walked from corridor to corridor to reach the office. On the way, we were met with high ranking officers as well as privates. Every time one of these soldiers saw me, they stopped and saluted me.

16.speaker: Player
16.text: ”This must be something serious. Especially since you invited me here.“

17.speaker: Player
17.text: ”Where is Valken? He usually partakes in all military meetings.“

18.speaker: Iosef Lancea
18.text: ”Valken is busy at the moment overseeing the defensive strategies against Rumburg.“

19.speaker: Iosef Lancea
19.text: ”It is important that you don't get misinformed on this matter. Valken has another agenda.“

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: When we finally arrived at Iosef's office, his entourage saluted us and left. He closed the door and took a seat.

22.speaker: Iosef Lancea
22.text: ”The situation with Rumburg is getting worse and our lack of funding in the military means that we would fight for survival in a war scenario.“

26.speaker: Iosef Lancea
26.text: ”The situation with Rumburg is getting worse and if it wasn't for our investments in the military, I would be even more concerned.“

27.speaker: Player
27.text: ”We are prepared for the worst aren't we, Iosef?“

28.speaker: Player
28.text: ”Your tone doesn't inspire confidence in our defensive capabilities.“

29.speaker: Player
29.text: ”Our soldiers are surely better motivated than theirs. We will defend our country!“

30.speaker: Player
30.text: ”What are our options in improving the situation?“

31.speaker: Iosef Lancea
31.text: ”Truthfully not fully prepared. We are still going through a few changes in the military to be able to confront them if such day was to arrive.“

32.speaker: Iosef Lancea
32.text: ”Our projected capability in the future should restore your confidence but we need to pass several changes to achieve a better situation.“

33.speaker: Iosef Lancea
33.text: ”Our efforts to restructure the military should prove beneficial in a potential conflict.“

37.speaker: Iosef Lancea
37.text: ”Since we refrained from modernising our military, the traditional force structure would have to match the enemies numbers.“

38.speaker: Iosef Lancea
38.text: ”We would never be able to match the force of Rumburg on equal terms therefore our switch of the military to a smaller, well-equipped and autonomously led combat units will prove better in the field.“

39.speaker: Player
39.text: ”You have been doing a fantastic job, Iosef. The military is in good hands.“

40.speaker: Player
40.text: ”I trust that you will defend the country if it comes to the worst.“

41.speaker: Iosef Lancea
41.text: ”Rumburg has superior numbers which we can't ever hope to match. The terrain is in our favour but once we cram hundreds of thousands in the mountains logistics will collapse.“

42.speaker: Iosef Lancea
42.text: ”The mandatory conscription law has become a matter of discussion and we need to strike a decision whether to keep it or remove it.“

43.speaker: Narrator
43.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Agnolia_Alliance"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_DefendBorder"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_JointOperation"] == true) == false)

44.speaker: Player
44.text: ”Whatever is necessary for our survival will be done when the time comes.“

45.speaker: Player
45.text: ”Isn't Valken the supporter of the quantity over quality approach?“

50.speaker: Valken Kruger
50.text: ”Why haven't I been invited? What is going on here?“

51.speaker: Iosef Lancea
51.text: ”There is no question in the motivation of our armed forces. However we must rely on the reality of the situation, especially when it is a matter of national survival.“

52.speaker: Iosef Lancea
52.text: ”We are making all the necessary preparations but any substantial military support from other nations would be a welcome deterrent against Rumburg.“

53.speaker: Player
53.text: ”Throwing bodies at a problem never solved it. Not sure if this is the right approach.“

54.speaker: Player
54.text: ”This doctrine worked for decades so far, no reason to change it. I think the generals have a point.“

55.speaker: Iosef Lancea
55.text: ”I am doing my best to defend the country. There is nothing I care for more than Sordland.“

56.speaker: Iosef Lancea
56.text: ”Let's hope it doesn't come to that.“

57.speaker: Iosef Lancea
57.text: ”We have never failed to defend this nation from invaders. We won't start now.“

58.speaker: Iosef Lancea
58.text: ”With no disrespect to him but he thinks that you can outgun the enemy but when fighting a larger force outsmarting them is what matters.“

62.speaker: Iosef Lancea
62.text: ”It is the last step remaining to switch to a modern professional armed force.“

63.speaker: Player
63.text: ”Remove mandatory conscription. It is time to have a professional force of willingly enlisted soldiers.“

64.speaker: Player
64.text: ”Are reservists really that damaging to the professional armed forces?“

65.speaker: Player
65.text: ”If they are a hindrance then we should remove mandatory conscription.“

66.speaker: Iosef Lancea
66.text: ”It will be a bloodbath for both sides.“

67.speaker: Player
67.text: ”Keep mandatory conscription. We need every single able body to defend the nation.“

68.speaker: Iosef Lancea
68.text: ”Sure. The new changes will be implemented as you wish.“

69.speaker: Iosef Lancea
69.text: ”Mr. President, I thought I explained it. Please rethink-.“

70.speaker: Iosef Lancea
70.text: ”We need all of our resources concentrated on our efficient units that will outperform the enemy in our mountainous terrain.“

71.speaker: Iosef Lancea
71.text: ”To truly modernise our fighting force we need to rid ourselves of the sluggish and inefficient cadets thrown to the ranks.“

72.speaker: Valken Kruger
72.text: ”Well we can't have less troops on the front-line than the enemy. Not with our current structure focused on mass mobilisation.“

73.speaker: Valken Kruger
73.text: ”I agree any huge structural change would be too late and too little now.“

75.speaker: Valken Kruger
75.text: ”I mean no disrespect but I am leading the ground operations and I must be informed of any strategic changes.“

76.speaker: Player
76.text: ”Well. Now that you are here, what is your opinion on conscription?“

77.speaker: Iosef Lancea
77.text: ”Our restructuring is hindered by a hundred thousands of cadets extending our logistics, slowing command structure and reducing the combat efficiency of our experienced units.“

78.speaker: Player
78.text: ”The Minister of Defense is your superior and so am I.“

79.speaker: Valken Kruger
79.text: ”Thank you, Mr. President. We are talking about our national defense which must be consulted among all staff.“

80.speaker: Iosef Lancea
80.text: ”To clarify, we would have brought the subject up with the General Staff and you.“

81.speaker: Iosef Lancea
81.text: ”It depends if this is the President's wish.“

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: Valken left with a hard salute.

84.speaker: Player
84.text: ”Expand the Air Force. We need more planes for air superiority.“

85.speaker: Player
85.text: ”Expand the Army. We need more soldiers to defend our nation.“

86.speaker: Player
86.text: ”Expand the Navy. We need to increase the amount of our ships.“

87.speaker: Player
87.text: ”Modernise the Navy. We need a higher-tech navy.“

88.speaker: Player
88.text: ”Modernise the Army. We need better equipped soldiers.“

89.speaker: Player
89.text: ”Modernise the Air Force. We need a better air force.“

93.speaker: Player
93.text: ”Agreed. There is a place for reservists.“

94.speaker: Player
94.text: ”We don't share the same opinion. This is a modern age and requires a modern army.“

95.speaker: Valken Kruger
95.text: ”The matter is rather simple from my point of view.“

99.speaker: Valken Kruger
99.text: ”Our forces have undergone large structural changes changing the operational capabilities and tactics.“

100.speaker: Valken Kruger
100.text: ”We kept to our traditional army doctrine. It is not devoid of disadvantages.“

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: I left the Ministry of Defense and returned to the Maroon Palace.

102.speaker: Valken Kruger
102.text: ”However, at the end of the day Rumburg has a larger army, air-force and navy. Our conscripts will fill the much needed weaknesses we have.“

103.speaker: Iosef Lancea
103.text: ”We also have to decide how exactly we spend our additional remaining funds in the military.“

104.speaker: Iosef Lancea
104.text: ”Let me look over my documents to see if there is anything else of concern.“

105.speaker: Iosef Lancea
105.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Military_Budget_Decrease"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_RumburgBorderReinforcement_DontReinforce"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Military_Budget_Decrease"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_RumburgBorderReinforcement_DontReinforce"] == true) == false)

109.speaker: Iosef Lancea
109.text: ”I don't think it is wise to change course now.“

113.speaker: Iosef Lancea
113.text: "Mr. President, we need to prioritize quality over quantity."

114.speaker: Player
114.text: ”Revert the removal of mandatory conscription. That is my final decision.“

115.speaker: Player
115.text: ”No. I am content with the decision.“

122.speaker: Iosef Lancea
122.text: ”In June we decided to upgrade the equipment of our military.“

123.speaker: Valken Kruger
123.text: ”The military thanks the administration for the extensive support.“

124.speaker: Iosef Lancea
124.text: ”In June we decided to expand the military.“

128.speaker: Iosef Lancea
128.text: ”We need to decide what branch we would want to expand further.“

129.speaker: Iosef Lancea
129.text: ”The military thanks the administration for the extensive support especially in creating a modern fighting force.“

130.speaker: Player
130.text: ”Which branch requires the expansion the most?“

131.speaker: Player
131.text: ”The Army could be enlarged and match the force size of most neighbours.“

133.speaker: Iosef Lancea
133.text: ”Strategically speaking the army would be the safest choice. However, the air and naval forces would do well with expansion too.“

134.speaker: Iosef Lancea
134.text: ”As you wish. The changes will be implemented this month and finished at the end of November.“

136.speaker: Iosef Lancea
136.text: ”Each branch would give us an advantage. Our military is larger overall but we can expand the Army, Air Force or Navy even further.“

137.speaker: Player
137.text: ”The Air Force expansion could give us the battlefield advantage.“

138.speaker: Iosef Lancea
138.text: ”The Air Force would welcome the addition of new fighters and bombers. The air is the new front.“

139.speaker: Player
139.text: ”The Navy expansion could protect us from a possible naval incursion.“

140.speaker: Iosef Lancea
140.text: ”Our nation has a long coast any naval expansion would protect our sea zone.“

141.speaker: Iosef Lancea
141.text: ”That's about it. I won't take more of your time sir.“

144.speaker: Valken Kruger
144.text: ”Strategically speaking the army would be the safest choice. However, the air and naval forces would do well with expansion too.“

145.speaker: Player
145.text: ”Which branch requires the expansion the most?“

146.speaker: Valken Kruger
146.text: ”The Air Force would welcome the addition of new fighters and bombers. The air is the new front.“

147.speaker: Player
147.text: ”The Army could be enlarged and match the force size of most neighbours.“

148.speaker: Valken Kruger
148.text: ”Our nation has a long coast any naval expansion would protect our sea zone.“

149.speaker: Player
149.text: ”The Navy expansion could protect us from a possible naval incursion.“

150.speaker: Player
150.text: ”The Air Force expansion could give us the battlefield advantage.“

151.speaker: Valken Kruger
151.text: ”We need to decide what branch we would want to expand.“

152.speaker: Iosef Lancea
152.text: ”We need to decide what branch we would want to modernise more.“

153.speaker: Iosef Lancea
153.text: ”Our nation has a long coast, a naval modernisation would protect our sea zone. This would be important, especially now that the Heljiland situation between Agnolia and Valgsland is likely to escalate.“

154.speaker: Iosef Lancea
154.text: ”The Air Force would welcome the addition of modern fighters and bombers. The air is the new front.“

155.speaker: Player
155.text: ”Which branch requires the modernisation the most?“

156.speaker: Iosef Lancea
156.text: ”Strategically speaking the army would be the safest choice. However, the air and naval forces would do well with further modernisation too.“

157.speaker: Player
157.text: ”The Navy modernisation could protect us from a possible naval incursion.“

158.speaker: Player
158.text: ”The Air Force modernisation could give us the battlefield advantage.“

159.speaker: Player
159.text: ”The Army could be modernised and match the quality of most neighbours.“

161.speaker: Narrator
161.text: I left the Ministry of Defense and returned to the Maroon Palace.

162.speaker: Narrator
162.text: I arrived at the cubic building that housed most of the military command that resided in Holsord. The grey and brutalist structure looked daunting.

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: I never liked this building. It always made me feel like I was standing under the concrete foot of a giant getting ready to crush me. It made me feel small and I never quite got used to the feeling even after this many years.

165.speaker: Narrator
165.text: He leaned back and interlocked his hands.

166.speaker: Player
166.text: ”I will make sure it won't come to that.“

167.speaker: Iosef Lancea
167.text: ”Not everything might be up to us, sir.“

168.speaker: Iosef Lancea
168.text: ”Not everything might be up to us, sir.“

169.speaker: Player
169.text: ”I will make sure it won't come to that.“

173.speaker: Iosef Lancea
173.text: ”The recent military partnership we have signed with Agnolia includes a mutual-defense clause.“

174.speaker: Iosef Lancea
174.text: ”In case of conflict we will be obliged to come to each others aid. In case of a Rumburg invasion, they will come for help.“

175.speaker: Player
175.text: ”Do you think their support would be enough to hold the line?“

177.speaker: Iosef Lancea
177.text: ”These are challenging times for us. Rumburg is a vulture circling around the region.“

178.speaker: Player
178.text: ”It is a disgrace that we have to rely on other nations for our defense.“

180.speaker: Iosef Lancea
180.text: ”Sure, Agnolia is better than nothing but we must look further. Lespia or Valgsland are options in my opinion.“

181.speaker: Iosef Lancea
181.text: ”Any deterrence should force them to think twice.“

182.speaker: Player
182.text: ”Do you really think that is absolutely necessary?“

183.speaker: Player
183.text: ”Advice noted. I will bring it up to Deivid.“

184.speaker: Iosef Lancea
184.text: ”Yes, it is. The danger far outweighs the sacrifice.“

185.speaker: Player
185.text: ”Sordland stands alone as always, Iosef. We won't rely on help from anyone else.“

186.speaker: Iosef Lancea
186.text: ”I think the same way however, I am tasked with our nations defense. We need to look at the situation realistically.“

188.speaker: Iosef Lancea
188.text: ”Me too but we might not have a choice.“

190.speaker: Iosef Lancea
190.text: ”Me too but we might not have a choice.“

191.speaker: Player
191.text: ”Let's wait for Valken before we make a decision. I wanna hear his viewpoint.“

192.speaker: Iosef Lancea
192.text: ”Mr. President, I don't think that will be necessary. He won't be comi-“

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: I thought for a moment before making my decision.

194.speaker: Valken Kruger
194.text: ”What is the meaning of this?! Iosef?“

196.speaker: Valken Kruger
196.text: ”I see what is going on here.“

197.speaker: Valken Kruger
197.text: ”Disappointing. So this is how the administration conducts matters on military affairs.“

198.speaker: Narrator
198.text: Valken looked furiously in my eyes.

201.speaker: Narrator
201.text: Iosef threw an angry look at Valken before turning to me.

217.speaker: Iosef Lancea
217.text: ”The Kruger fortification line in construction should help us in the defense of the mountainous and hilly provinces and at the worst case delay a potential advance.“

224.speaker: Iosef Lancea
224.text: ”As a result of the recent deal with Wehlen, we have started reinforcing the border.“

225.speaker: Iosef Lancea
225.text: ”Forward scouts have been deployed and we have started moving our divisions.“

226.speaker: Iosef Lancea
226.text: ”Rest assured. We are ready for anything that will come from the other side of the border.“

227.speaker: Iosef Lancea
227.text: ”We will be providing our reports to you.“

228.speaker: Player
228.text: ”I don't think we will have any problems but stay alert. We don't know what we are dealing with yet.“

229.speaker: Player
229.text: ”I don't want anyone in. Do not let a single deserter pass our borders.“

230.speaker: Player
230.text: ”Try to be lenient if possible. There might be people who are simply trying to escape war among them.“

231.speaker: Iosef Lancea
231.text: ”We are always ready for any situation, Mr. President.“

234.speaker: Iosef Lancea
234.text: ”As a result of the recent deal with Wehlen, we have started organising the troops for the joint operation.“
234.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Agnolia_Alliance"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_DefendBorder"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_JointOperation"] == true)

235.speaker: Iosef Lancea
235.text: ”General Valken and I were discussing the war plan.“

236.speaker: Iosef Lancea
236.text: ”12th battalion of the 3rd Army, along with air support units, will do the job.“

237.speaker: Iosef Lancea
237.text: ”We will meet up with the Wehzek military command to discuss our joint strategy.“

238.speaker: Player
238.text: ”Excellent. I will be waiting for the results.“

239.speaker: Player
239.text: ”Show them the might of the Sordish Armed Forces.“

240.speaker: Player
240.text: ”Be wary. I don't trust Wiktor Smolak even a little bit, nor his army.“

241.speaker: Iosef Lancea
241.text: ”You will be provided with our reports.“

242.speaker: Iosef Lancea
242.text: ”We are always ready for any situation, Mr. President.“

243.speaker: Iosef Lancea
243.text: ”The entire world will see, Mr. President. Don't doubt it.“

244.speaker: Iosef Lancea
244.text: ”Let's move on to our main topic.“

261.speaker: Player
261.text: ”Remove mandatory conscription. It is time to have a professional force of willingly enlisted soldiers.“

265.speaker: Player
265.text: ”Keep mandatory conscription. We need every single able body to defend the nation.“

361.speaker: Iosef Lancea
361.text: ”The facts are that the conscription gives us a large reservist pool that can cover a larger frontline but these troops lack the morale and quality to be offensive elements.“

362.speaker: Iosef Lancea
362.text: ”My argument would be to remove conscription if our military can stand on it's own two feet without them. If we are going to have strong allies why do we need conscripts?“

394.speaker: Player
394.text: ”Please leave us to conduct the meeting in private, Valken.“

395.speaker: Player
395.text: ”Tell me what you think, General Kruger.“
